Maya Chen: Quick heads-up — depscanner flagged CVE-2025-4321 (libfastio) affecting transcode svc. I realized our intake->routing->ownership path is kinda ad-hoc. Can we sketch a short runbook here?
Jordan Patel: +1. Recommend a fast-path: score >=7 OR exploit observed => immediate oncall notify + triage channel + assign owner.
sec-bot: New vuln ticket created: VULN-2025-4321. Status: open. Severity: 8.1. Affected: transcode-service, ingestion-worker.
Chris Ross: High-level principle: service owners do the patch work, Security coordinates cross-service, KMS and RBAC reviews, and approves emergency key rotations.
Olivia Nguyen: For KMS integrations — if secret material is implicated, we should default to short-lived credentials + rotate CMKs only if evidence shows key compromise. Need a checklist.
Maya Chen: Draft runbook idea (one-line steps, to be expanded):
```
1) Confirm CVE details and public exploit status
2) Identify affected images/packages and delta windows
3) Assign component owner + security liaison (fast-path assignment)
4) Apply short-term mitigations (config toggles, traffic filters)
5) Prepare patch/backport + CI smoke tests + canary plan
6) Schedule KMS/RBAC actions if secrets/keys in scope
7) Verify audit logs and increase retention/verbosity for 7 days
8) Rollout, monitor, rollback plan ready
9) Postmortem and CVE tracker update
```
Jordan Patel: Also add a quick prioritization matrix: public exploit OR active PoC => P0. Prod-facing customer-impacting services => up-prioritize to P0/P1. Internal tooling with no external impact => P2.
Andrew Lee: I can be oncall owner for the next 48h for this ticket. @Maya Chen assign to me for coordination.
Olivia Nguyen: Who signs off emergency RBAC changes? We should have a preapproved emergency RBAC template + audit steps so teams can act quickly without waiting hours for manual approval.
Chris Ross: I'll draft a template IAM policy for emergency elevation and add a short approval flow (security + infra lead) — link back here when done.
Maya Chen: Good. Also we should standardize: when KMS rotation is required, Security will: create temp key, re-encrypt short-lived secrets, execute rotation window, then rotate old CMK out after 72h monitoring. Olivia, can you draft that?
Olivia Nguyen: Yep — will write a one-page KMS rotation checklist: pre-checks, rotation steps, rollback, and audit queries to run. Target: 4h.
Jordan Patel: Add metrics to the runbook: time-to-first-mitigation, time-to-patch-merge, time-to-full-rollout. These are the SLA knobs for Dedicated customers.
Maya Chen: Action items: Andrew create wiki runbook and link the ticket (due in 2h), Chris add RBAC templates (due EOD), Olivia write KMS rotation checklist (due 4h), Jordan formalize prioritization matrix (due EOD). Security: I'll maintain the tracker. Ping here if blocked.
sec-bot: :white_check_mark: VULN-2025-4321 assigned to Andrew Lee (oncall).
Chris Ross: ack
Olivia Nguyen: ack
Andrew Lee: ack — starting intake now. Will post initial mitigation in ticket in 30m.
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll iterate the runbook after the first real incident to make it leaner.
